name: multi-hop
description: Questions that span two concerns, each built on a twin pair whose vocabulary overlaps (the corpus's own distractor law: a doc leaking neighbor vocabulary steals that neighbor's query). Single-pass retrieval leads with the first half's vocabulary; the agentic loop decomposes into independent sub-queries and fuses every leg ON TOP of the bilingual fused order. Measured A/B (2026-11-18): fixture parity (5/5 both ways, MRR 0.70 single and looped); production-corpus A/B mixed (one real-query rescued 0->1, one regressed 2->0 — naive RRF over heterogeneous legs dilutes), so the loop ships opt-in with this suite as its non-regression gate and the usage eval as its judge.

cases.question: When a duplicate lands, the write path absorbs it into the oldest row — and which later pass re-reads the related band to stamp same, supersede or distinct verdicts?
The extraction concurrency defaults to one turn at a time against a single runner — and separately, why do breaker-open rejections leave a turn's attempt counter untouched?
Chat generations hold their own dedicated HTTP client — and inside KAP itself, why does a plain timeout placed before retry never get retried?
The vector leg's index can be defeated by a semi-join — and how do the two rank lists fuse so an exact token match rescues a chunk the embedding underweights?
Salience decays with a thirty-day half-life and floors classify the memory — and which three edge kinds connect memories so a search can surface what the query never named?
